newsitem.title: USA: Comcast, at +275 to +300, tops US high-yld issues.
newsitem.headline: Comcast, at +275 to +300, tops US high-yld issues.

text.p: Comfortable cash flows in U.S. high-yield mutual funds will be a boon to issuers of junk bonds this week, which will be topped by an expected $900 million 10-year non-callable debt from Comcast Cellular Holdings, market sources said.
Price talk on the deal ranges from 275 to 300 basis points off the Treasury curve, one fund manager said.

Proceeds from the deal will be used to redeem all zero coupon notes and repay some outstanding bank debt of Comcast Cellular Corp. Comcast Cellular Holdings is a newly formed holding company and unit of Comcast Corp.
"At 2-7/8 off this strikes me as being a pretty good deal," said one junk bond fund manager, adding that the deal's size and promise of good liquidity are also positives.

Ratings on the deal, at B2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB-plus by Standard & Poor's, are unusually divergent. The primary difference, buyside sources said, is the treatment of a contribution of Comcast Cellular bonds from Comcast Corp to the cellular subsidiary -- S&P treats it as cash equity contribution whereas Moody's does not.
Despite the divided rating, the deal is nonetheless seen attractive at the bandied about price talk.

Comcast Cellular is expected to price the deal, which was restructured last week to shorten the maturity from 12 to 10 years, will be priced in the 144A market on Monday afternoon via lead manager Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, market sources said.
High-yield deals will reap benefits of three consecutive weeks of inflows to junk bond funds that included $760 million in the latest recording week, dealers and investors said.
In fact, investors noted improved market tone and cash flows allowed the success of some aggressively priced paper seen late last week.

At 10-5/8 percent yield, Friday's $100 million senior subordinated notes from American Builders & Contractors Supply deal appeared rich for the privately-held company, according to one fund manager. But the par-price deal still traded higher when freed to trade, recently quoted at 101.

Other junk issues set to price this week include: $300 million seven-year senior notes from Cityscape Financial Corp, $230 million 10-year senior secured notes from GST Telecom Inc, $100 million 10-year senior secured notes from French Fragrances Inc, and $100 million 10-year senior secured notes from Western Star Holdings Ltd.
Turning to investment grades, issuance features DR Investment's $800 million five- and 10-year debt early in the week, according to lead manager Lehman Brothers.
DR Investment is a unit of Dominion Resources. Proceeds from the deal will replace bridge financing in connection with Dominion's acquisition of East Midlands Electricity Plc, the company said.
Elsewhere, Mellon Bank Corp will tap the primary market with a $300 million debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston sometime this week, the manager said.
The A2/A-rated deal is expected to consist of a 10-year maturity with price talk seen at between 68 and 70 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries, sources said.
Norfolk Southern Corp's $3 billion multi-tranche issue may be priced next week, sources said.
